learningObjective: See how an i.i.d. exponential-family sample collapses to a fixed-size summed sufficient statistic and why an interior MLE matches its empirical moment to the model moment.
mediumRationale: A compact deterministic SVG can show six raw Bernoulli observations collapsing to one count, substitute that count into the sample log-likelihood, and align the empirical and model moments at the MLE without requiring interaction.

mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a table can list the derivation but does not make the many-to-one compression from a growing sample to a fixed-dimensional statistic as immediate.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: changing the observations or Bernoulli parameter adds controls without improving the central sufficiency and score-equation argument.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: no authoritative source figure with verified reuse permission isolates this exact Bernoulli compression-to-moment-match lesson; the implementation is an original worked schematic.

pages.insight: The Basic Probabilistic ML Algorithms divider begins the only deck neighborhood that explicitly names the exponential family.

The EM slide says exponential-family complete-data likelihoods reduce the E-step to expected sufficient statistics and can make M-step updates closed form, but it does not define canonical form or derive dataset sufficiency.
The neighboring graphical-models slide moves to factorization, conditional independence, and variable elimination, adding no exponential-family derivation.
The forward-backward and Baum-Welch slide provides later context for the EM claim on page 65 but does not discuss sufficient-statistic compression.
The CRF slide uses a log-partition function to normalize sequence scores, offering a concrete later use of the term but not its exponential-family derivative identities.
The next slide begins linear factor models and confirms that the deck has moved beyond the log-partition example.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed page-by-page for exponential family, sufficient statistic, natural parameter, log-partition, conjugate prior, Bernoulli, and Poisson. Page 65 is the only slide that explicitly names the exponential family and sufficient statistics; pages 64-66 were read as its contiguous neighborhood. Page 70 is the only other log-partition match, so pages 69-71 were also inspected. The deck supplies an EM use case and a CRF normalization use case, but no canonical-form derivation, dataset-compression visual, or moment-matching explanation. No deck image, wording, equation layout, or artwork is reused.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is the connection between sufficiency and moment matching. For i.i.d. observations, multiplying canonical-form densities makes every parameter-dependent data term pass through S = sum_i T(x_i), while the log-partition term becomes nA(eta). Differentiating gives S - n grad A(eta) = S - n E_eta[T(X)]; therefore an interior stationary MLE equates the empirical sufficient-statistic mean S/n with the model mean. The original figure uses six Bernoulli observations, S = 4, and p-hat = 4/6 as a fully checkable instance. It does not claim that an MLE always exists or is interior.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected both relevant neighborhoods, then checked two university statistics references before choosing an original Bernoulli sufficient-statistic and moment-matching derivation.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and a complete text description containing all six observations, the summed statistic, the sample log-likelihood, score equation, and result. Every stage is explicitly labelled and connected by arrow direction; the statistic uses a pill shape and the estimate uses a double-outlined result box, so the lesson does not depend on color. Its 360-pixel viewBox fits the established single-column visual panel without a minimum width, preserving readable labels at 390 CSS pixels. Existing theme variables provide dark-mode contrast and shared print tokens force a high-contrast light palette while keeping the figure together.
